headline: GOLD HOLDS $4,608, SILVER ENDS AT $68.99 — THIRD STRAIGHT WEEKLY GAIN; LATAM MINERS RALLY
snippet: Gold settled at $4,608 per ounce on Friday August 21, 2026 — a gain of 1.80% on the session — while silver closed at $68.99, up 1.15%, as both metals posted their third consecutive weekly advance. The move was powered by a softer US dollar, which makes dollar-priced metals cheaper for overseas buyers, and continued safe-haven demand tied to US debt concerns and slowing global growth. Gold is now up approximately 9% in August while silver has gained 14% for the month — the dual-demand dynamic of financial safe-haven flows stacking on top of industrial consumption (solar, EVs, AI data centers) keeping the silver outperformance trade intact. Latin American gold and silver miners, particularly those listed on the Mexican and Peruvian exchanges, gained in sympathy with spot on the August 21 session.

headline: BUNKER HILL + SILVER47 MERGE FOR 'MADE IN AMERICA' U.S. SILVER CHAMPION — 38% PREMIUM, ALL-STOCK DEAL
snippet: Bunker Hill Mining Corp. and Silver47 Exploration Corp. announced a definitive all-stock merger agreement dated August 20, 2026, creating a US-focused silver and critical minerals champion. Silver47 shareholders will receive 0.1724 Bunker Hill shares per share — implying approximately US$0.67 per Silver47 share, a 38% premium to the last closing price and a 30% premium to the 20-day VWAP. Post-merger, Bunker Hill shareholders own ~57% and Silver47 shareholders ~43% of the combined company, which will pursue a name change to 'Bunker Hill Silver Corp.' and retain its TSX listing. The deal combines the operating Bunker Hill Mine in Idaho's historic Silver Valley with Silver47's exploration pipeline in Alaska, Nevada, and New Mexico — positioning the combined entity as a domestic US silver supply chain alternative at a time of record-high silver prices above $68/oz. The transaction requires approval from Silver47 shareholders.

headline: COPPER FIRMS TO $6.58 ON WEAKER DOLLAR AND CHINA RESTOCKING — SUPPLY CASE REBUILDS AROUND CHILE, PERU
snippet: Copper advanced on August 21, 2026 to approximately $6.58 per pound at the global spot benchmark — recovering from the $6.50 pivot that held as support after the all-time record near $6.90 on August 6. Gains were powered by the US Dollar Index retreat (making dollar-priced metals more accessible for overseas buyers) and a renewed Chinese restocking bid tied to Beijing's promised infrastructure spending. The supply-side case continues to build around constrained production from Chile and Peru, even as near-term Chinese demand data remains mixed. The CPER copper-futures ETF gained 1.63% on the week. The pending US Commerce Department tariff ruling on copper imports — still unissued despite an original June deadline — remains the most significant near-term price catalyst for the metal.

headline: SELKIRK COPPER HITS 13.12% CuEq AT MINTO NORTH — YUKON RESTART PEA ON TRACK FOR Q3 2026
snippet: Selkirk Copper Mines Inc. (TSXV: SCMI) released additional Phase 2 drill results from the former Minto copper-gold-silver mine in Yukon, Canada on August 20, 2026. Highlight intercept 26SCM190 at Minto North returned 6.01% Cu, 8.77 g/t Au, and 36.6 g/t Ag (13.12% CuEq) over 1.93 metres within a broader 33.2-metre interval at 1.49% CuEq. Step-out hole 26SCM205 at Minto North added 3.43% Cu, 0.36 g/t Au, and 47 g/t Ag (3.87% CuEq) over 3.7 metres within 13.3 metres at 2.25% CuEq. At Area 118, 125 metres from historic underground development, 26SCM188 returned 3.39% Cu, 0.61 g/t Au, and 16.5 g/t Ag (3.73% CuEq) over 6.0 metres. The 50,000-metre Phase 2 program is 90% complete (45,299m in 187 holes as of August 18); a preliminary economic assessment targeting a Minto mine restart is on track for Q3 2026.

headline: MINRES BALD HILL LITHIUM FY27 GUIDANCE DUE AUG 27 — 18-MONTH RESTART ON TRACK; CORE LITHIUM FINNISS ALSO RAMPING
snippet: Mineral Resources Ltd. (ASX: MIN) will release detailed FY27 guidance for its restarted Bald Hill lithium mine in Western Australia on August 27, 2026 — five days from now — covering expected sales volumes, free-on-board costs, and capital expenditure for the 165,000 dry metric tonne per year spodumene concentrate operation. The Bald Hill restart, triggered by lithium prices rising 84.56% year-over-year to CNY 152,250 per tonne, began physical production in July 2026 after an 18-month care-and-maintenance period; approximately 370 new jobs are being created. The August 27 guidance disclosure will be the first detailed economic read on Bald Hill's restart economics — a key signal for the lithium sector and for other Australian operations that also restarted on the price recovery, including Core Lithium's Finniss project, which awarded a A$50 million mining contract to NRW Holdings in May 2026 with first concentrate targeted for the September–December 2026 quarter.

headline: USA RARE EARTH SERRA VERDE VOTE IN 6 DAYS — $2.8B BRAZIL HEAVY RARE EARTH DEAL EXPECTED Q3 CLOSE
snippet: USA Rare Earth (NYSE: USAR) shareholders vote on August 28, 2026 — six days from today — on whether to approve the company's $2.8 billion acquisition of Serra Verde Group, owner of the operating Pela Ema rare earth mine and processing plant in Goiás, Brazil. The deal, announced April 20, consists of $300 million cash plus approximately 126.8 million newly issued USAR shares. Serra Verde produces heavy rare earth elements including NdPr, dysprosium, and terbium — the magnets-critical materials where Western supply chains remain most exposed to China's export controls. The acquisition would make USA Rare Earth one of the largest non-Chinese integrated rare earth suppliers globally. USAR held approximately $1.5 billion in cash at last report. Shareholder approval would trigger one of the most consequential Western rare earth supply chain transactions since Beijing's export controls began reshaping the sector.

headline: URANIUM EXPLORERS RACE FOR ATHABASCA HIGH-GRADE AS AI NUCLEAR DEMAND PUSHES SPOT TO $88.50
snippet: A Streetwise Reports roundup published August 20, 2026 highlights uranium explorers advancing high-grade targets in the Athabasca Basin of Saskatchewan, the world's highest-grade uranium district, against a backdrop of structurally tightening supply and surging AI-driven power demand. CanAlaska Uranium confirmed uranium mineralization along the C10S corridor at its West McArthur Project from 2026 winter drilling, supporting the potential for additional high-grade zones in partnership with Cameco. Uranium spot prices held at approximately $88.50 per pound — up 21% year-over-year — as US utilities lock in long-term supply contracts to underpin nuclear baseload for AI datacenter electricity demand projected to reach 580 TWh by 2028. Kazatomprom reported a 9% year-on-year increase in Kazakhstan uranium production in the first half of 2026, yet institutional consensus holds that mined supply will cover less than 75% of future reactor requirements.

headline: KALKINE: PAN AMERICAN SILVER, IAMGOLD, ENDEAVOUR — 4 GOLD STOCKS TO WATCH AT $4,608 GOLD
snippet: Kalkine's August 2026 round-up examines four gold and silver mining names worth watching as gold trades near $4,608: Pan American Silver (TSX: PAAS), which offers leveraged silver exposure and a freshly completed acquisition; Alamos Gold (TSX: AGI), a Canada-heavy grower that is 'nursing a production wobble' from the Young-Davidson seismic event but delivers one of the clearest organic growth stories via the Island Gold mine ramp-up; IAMGOLD (TSX: IMG), which has spent two years transforming its balance sheet around the giant Côté Gold mine in Ontario while carrying political risk in Burkina Faso; and Endeavour Mining, a West Africa-focused senior miner. The piece identifies a sector paradox: while record gold prices above $4,500 enrich miners, operational and geopolitical uncertainties prevent full re-rating — the paradox where value lives.

headline: SEEKINGALPHA: 15 GOLD AND SILVER MINERS STILL MISPRICED — 'LOW-HANGING FRUIT' AT RECORD GOLD PRICES
snippet: A Seeking Alpha analysis from August 2026 identifies 15 gold and silver mining stocks it classifies as 'low-hanging fruit' — names where the stock re-rating has materially lagged the earnings improvement driven by gold trading above $4,500 and silver above $65 per ounce. The analysis documents the persistent valuation discount embedded in the sector, consistent with the pattern noted by WisdomTree, GoldSeek's Adam Hamilton, and multiple buy-side analysts: gold and silver equities have not fully priced in the sustained margin expansion from a gold price that has risen roughly 80% over the prior 18 months while all-in sustaining costs have risen far less. For retail investors in junior and mid-tier miners, the piece provides a screening framework for identifying companies where the re-rating still has the most runway.

headline: GOLDSEEK GOLD SWOT: EVOLUTION MINING EXPANDS COPPER PIPELINE AS GOLD CASH FLOW FUNDS NEXT GROWTH CYCLE
snippet: GoldSeek's weekly Gold SWOT report (published around August 21, 2026) highlights Evolution Mining's move to expand its copper growth pipeline — a signpost of a broader trend in which mid-tier gold miners are leveraging record cash flow, generated by gold above $4,500 per ounce, to diversify into copper assets and extend their project pipelines. The Gold SWOT framework reveals the structural opportunity in the sector: senior gold and silver producers have now paid out a record annualized $10.9 billion in dividends and share buybacks in 2026, already surpassing 2025's full-year record of $8.6 billion, yet sector P/E multiples remain compressed relative to the earnings base. Evolution Mining's copper push demonstrates how the strongest operators are recycling record profits into the next growth cycle rather than returning all capital — a strategy that may widen the gap between leaders and laggards as the gold bull market matures.
